points.text: Unclear whether quality scores come from 1v3 (MTI) or 1v1 (PDTS) setting.
Score differences between Table 2 and Table 3 unexplained.
Role of SFT student model unclear; gains may reflect familiarity with training students.
Student profiles identically distributed in train and test; OOD generalization untested.
Two-stage split (1v3 vs 1v1) for data and training not justified.
Differentiated instruction present in DPO but absent in SFT data; unexplained.
1024-token DPO max length may be insufficient for long dialogues.
Unclear whether datasets simulate one-to-many classroom or one-on-one dialogues.
Quality of student agent simulation not evaluated.
Human evaluators' qualifications not described.
Stated challenges (questioning disrupting flow, stage-adaptive questioning) not addressed.
SFT+DPO validation cannot separate dataset quality from training effects.
Base model for training EduDial not stated.
Human-machine evaluation discussion insufficient; human assessment bias not ruled out.
No calibration with real teachers and students; classroom realism unproven.
No learner outcome evidence; only ratings of simulated dialogues.
Rubric rewards surface behaviours like frequent questioning.
Ability-label differentiation has equity risks; no bias analysis.
Judge validation uses model-mean correlation only; large cell-level gaps.
Expert qualifications and inter-rater agreement not given.
Fixed Bloom stage script does not address adaptive questioning timing.
Data provenance, licensing and dialogue language not stated.
Hyperparameters selected by grid search on the test set.
'Outperforms all baselines on all metrics' contradicted by several dimensions.
Circular evaluation: shared rubric/prompts, GPT-4o verifies and judges, o1 generates and competes.
Student models used at evaluation unspecified.
Missing controls: same base on other corpora, scaffold-prompted baselines.
No variance reported; small human margin.
10-point AIME drop described as slight.
34,250 sessions conflates dialogues and preference pairs.
'Authentic classroom interactions' claimed for o1-generated text.
Scope limited to mathematics.
Baseline count 18 vs 17.
MT-Bench citation wrong; SocraticLM listed twice.
DPO equations lack beta and reference policy.
Table 3 base AVG inconsistent with Table 2.
Abstract overstates Table 2; content coverage below baselines.
Benchmark claim weak: no fixed test suite, unspecified simulators, no run noise.
Table 2 dense without highlighting; Table 3 rater unstated.
Reasoning drop in Table 4 framed acceptable; correctness not measured.
Baseline count, section heading, typos.
No limitations section.
Novelty versus prior corpora (MathDial, SocraticLM) asserted without comparison.
No same-base, same-recipe training on competing data to show data quality.
Pedagogical grounding thin: Bloom mapping order, strategy derivation undocumented.
Authentic classroom claim unsupported; no comparison with real transcripts.
Student levels are model-size proxies, not validated cognitive profiles.
Scope broader in wording than content: math only, one base model.
Citation inaccuracies: MT-Bench, duplicated SocraticLM, DPO uncited, AlpacaEval.
Hyperparameters tuned on the test set producing all reported numbers.
Abstract claim of outperforming on all metrics contradicted by Table 2.
Table 3 irreconcilable with Table 2; rater type unstated.
No variance, seeds or uncertainty on comparisons.
AIME drop called within expected range without basis.
Baseline prompts, decoding and API versions unstated; fairness undefined.
Test students may be training simulators, favouring EduDial-LLM.
Missing same-base-other-data and template-prompted baseline controls.
DPO equations do not match described objective; DPO uncited.
Baseline count, heading, lost percent sign.
34,250 sessions includes preference pairs.

P.summary: Table 2 vs Table 3 score differences unexplained.
Evaluation students same as training students; familiarity confound.
Differentiated teaching asymmetric between SFT and DPO data.
Max sequence length may be too short.
Dataset contribution not separated from training effects.
No validation against real classroom data.

Q.summary: Fixed stage script vs adaptive questioning.
Overclaim of outperforming on all metrics.
Evaluation students unspecified or same as training simulators.
Session count conflates dialogues and pairs.
Scope: math only, one base model.
Table 3 inconsistent with Table 2; rater unstated.
